easy.def: A clear, hard jewel.
examples: The ring has a diamond.
A diamond sparkles.
The diamond is clear.

more.def: A very hard, clear jewel that sparkles in light.
examples: His ring was set with a diamond.
A diamond is the hardest natural material.
The crown was covered in diamonds.

easy.def: A shape with four sides like a tilted square.
examples: Draw a diamond.
The kite is a diamond.
The sign is a diamond.

more.def: A shape with four equal sides that looks like a tilted square.
examples: The kite was shaped like a diamond.
Draw a diamond on your paper.
The road sign was a yellow diamond.

easy.def: The field in baseball.
examples: Players ran onto the diamond.
The diamond has four bases.
The pitcher stands on the diamond.

more.def: The inside part of a baseball field, marked by four bases.
examples: The players ran onto the diamond.
The pitcher stood in the middle of the diamond.
Fans watched from behind the diamond.

easy.def: To stop living.
examples: Plants die without water.
The flower died.
Fish die out of water.

more.def: To stop being alive, as every living thing does one day.
examples: Some insects die when the weather turns cold.
The old tree died during the long drought.
Leaves die and fall to the ground in autumn.

easy.def: The food a person or animal usually eats.
examples: A panda's diet is bamboo.
I eat a healthy diet.
The doctor talked about diet.

more.def: The kinds of food that a person or animal usually eats.
examples: A panda's diet is mostly bamboo.
Fruit and vegetables are part of a healthy diet.
The vet talked about the dog's diet.

easy.def: How two things are not the same.
examples: What is the difference?
Find the difference.
There is a big difference.

more.def: A way in which two or more things are not alike.
examples: What is the difference between a frog and a toad?
One difference is that the red kite is bigger.
There is a big difference between hot and warm.

easy.def: Not the same.
examples: My socks are different colors.
We go to different schools.
This apple tastes different.

more.def: Not like something or someone else.
examples: The twins look alike, but they have very different hobbies.
People in different countries celebrate the new year in different ways.
My handwriting looks different when I use a pen.

easy.def: Hard to do.
examples: The puzzle is difficult.
It was a difficult test.
It was a difficult climb.

more.def: Not easy; needing a lot of effort or skill.
examples: The math problem was difficult, but I solved it.
It is difficult to ride a bike on ice.
Climbing the steep mountain was difficult.

easy.def: To make a hole in the ground.
examples: Dogs dig holes.
We dig in the sand.
He dug a hole.

more.def: To make a hole by moving earth with a tool or paws.
examples: The dog dug a hole under the fence.
We dug for clams at the beach.
Workers dig a trench for the pipes.

easy.def: A coin worth ten cents.
examples: I found a dime.
A dime is ten cents.
I put a dime in the jar.

more.def: A small coin worth ten cents.
examples: I found a dime under the couch.
Ten dimes make a dollar.
She paid for the sticker with two dimes.

easy.def: A small place to eat simple meals.
examples: We ate breakfast at a diner.
The diner serves pancakes.
The diner is open all night.

more.def: A small restaurant that serves simple meals, often with long counters.
examples: We ate pancakes at the diner.
The diner at the corner is famous for its milkshakes.
A waitress poured coffee at the diner counter.

easy.def: A person who is eating at a restaurant.
examples: The diner ordered soup.
The diners enjoyed the meal.
A diner waved to the waiter.

more.def: A person who is eating a meal in a restaurant.
examples: The diner ordered the soup of the day.
The diners enjoyed the fresh bread.
A diner asked the waiter for more water.

easy.def: The main meal of the day, eaten at night.
examples: We eat dinner at six.
Dinner is ready.
What is for dinner?

more.def: The main meal of the day, usually eaten in the evening.
examples: We set the table for dinner and sat down together.
Dad cooked a pot of soup for dinner.
My grandparents came over for dinner on Sunday.

easy.def: Straight, with no stops.
examples: We took a direct route.
A direct flight.
It is a direct line.

more.def: Going straight without turns or stops.
examples: We took the direct road to the beach.
There is a direct flight to Texas.
The path is direct and flat.

easy.def: To show the way.
examples: The guard directed us.
Direct traffic.
She directs the play.

more.def: To show the way or tell people what to do.
examples: The police officer directed traffic.
She directed the play.
He directed us to the library.

easy.def: The way something goes.
examples: Which direction is the park?
Go in that direction.
The wind changed direction.

more.def: The path or way that something goes or faces.
examples: Which direction should we hike?
The wind changed direction during the storm.
We walked in the direction of the lake.

easy.def: Instructions.
examples: Read the directions.
Follow the directions.
She gave me directions.

more.def: Words that tell you how to do something or how to get somewhere.
examples: Read the directions before you begin.
She gave us directions to the library.
Follow the directions on the box.

easy.def: A person who leads a play or movie.
examples: The director told the actors what to do.
The director shouted, "Action!"
The play director smiled.

more.def: A person who guides actors and makes a play or movie.
examples: The director told the actors where to stand.
The film director yelled, "Cut!"
Our play director gave us notes.

easy.def: A person in charge of a group.
examples: The museum director gave a talk.
The camp director welcomed us.
The director is kind.

more.def: A person who is in charge of a group, school or organization.
examples: The director of the museum gave a tour.
The camp director welcomed all the kids.
The orchestra director raised her baton.

easy.def: The earth on the ground that plants grow in.
examples: The dirt is muddy.
I dug in the dirt.
There was dirt on my shoes.

more.def: Loose soil, or any stuff that makes something unclean.
examples: The worms live in the dirt.
He washed the dirt off his hands.
A truck brought a load of dirt for the garden.

easy.def: Not clean.
examples: My shoes are dirty.
My boots are dirty and muddy.
The dog is dirty.

more.def: Covered with dirt, mud or stains; not clean.
examples: My shoes got dirty in the muddy field.
Put the dirty dishes in the sink.
The dog's paws were dirty.

easy.def: To go away so you can't see it.
examples: The sun will disappear behind the clouds.
My socks always disappear!
The rabbit disappeared into a hole.

more.def: To go out of sight or stop existing.
examples: The snow disappeared as soon as the weather warmed up.
The plane disappeared into the clouds.
The stain disappeared after we washed the shirt.

easy.def: To make someone sad because something did not happen.
examples: I do not want to disappoint my team.
The rain disappointed the kids.
I will try not to disappoint you.

more.def: To make someone unhappy by not doing what they hoped for or expected.
examples: The canceled trip disappointed the whole class.
The movie's ending disappointed many fans.
She did not want to disappoint her coach by quitting.

easy.def: Sad because something was not as good as you hoped.
examples: I was disappointed when it rained.
She was disappointed with her score.
He looked disappointed.

more.def: Sad or let down because something did not turn out the way you wanted.
examples: We were disappointed when the game was canceled.
She felt disappointed that her friend could not come.
The disappointed fans left the stadium quietly.

easy.def: A terrible event that causes much damage.
examples: The flood was a disaster.
The storm was a disaster.
The picnic was a disaster.

more.def: A sudden event that causes great harm or damage, such as a flood or fire.
examples: The flood was a disaster for the town.
Many people helped after the disaster.
Our picnic was a disaster because it rained.

easy.def: To find something for the first time.
examples: I discovered a tiny shell in the sand.
We discovered a nest in the tree.
He discovered he likes peas.

more.def: To find or learn something that you did not know about before.
examples: Scientists discovered a new kind of frog in the rainforest.
The hikers discovered a hidden waterfall.
I discovered that I am good at chess.

related.def: A person who finds something first.

easy.def: To talk about something with others.
examples: We discuss the book.
They discussed the plan.
Let us discuss it.

more.def: To talk about something with other people, to share ideas.
examples: The class discussed the story after reading it.
Let us discuss where to go for lunch.
The family discussed their vacation plans.

easy.def: A talk about something.
examples: We had a class discussion.
The discussion was about the park.
Everyone joined the discussion.

more.def: A talk in which people share ideas about something.
examples: We had a class discussion about the story.
The discussion lasted half an hour.
Everyone joined the discussion about the new rule.

easy.def: An illness.
examples: The disease spread.
Measles is a disease.
The doctor treats disease.

more.def: An illness that makes a person, animal or plant sick.
examples: Measles is a disease that spreads easily.
Washing your hands helps stop disease.
The tree died of a disease.

easy.def: Making you feel sick.
examples: The smell is disgusting.
That bug is disgusting.
The old milk was disgusting.

more.def: So unpleasant that it makes you feel sick.
examples: The rotten food in the fridge smelled disgusting.
I thought the dirty sock was disgusting.
The garbage truck left a disgusting smell on the street.

easy.def: A plate or bowl for food.
examples: Put the dish on the table.
I wash the dishes.
The dish is hot.

more.def: A flat or deep container that holds food, or the food made in it.
examples: She put a dish of salad on the table.
We washed the dishes after dinner.
Pasta is my favorite dish.

easy.def: To let someone go.
examples: The teacher dismissed the class.
She dismissed us at noon.
School is dismissed.

more.def: To tell people they may leave, or to decide not to think about something.
examples: The teacher dismissed the class at three o'clock.
The principal dismissed the students for lunch.
He dismissed the idea because it was silly.

easy.def: How far it is from one place to another.
examples: The distance to school is short.
We can see the hills in the distance.
I can throw the ball a long distance.

more.def: The amount of space between two places or things.
examples: The distance between our town and the ocean is two hundred miles.
The runners trained to race a distance of five miles.
From a distance, the two houses look exactly the same.

easy.def: To take someone's attention away from something.
examples: Noise can distract me.
The toy distracted the baby.
Do not distract the driver.

more.def: To pull someone's attention away from what they are doing.
examples: The loud noise distracted me from my work.
A toy distracted the baby from crying.
Please do not distract the bus driver.

easy.def: A part of a town or country.
examples: Our school district has ten schools.
The district is near the river.
The shopping district is busy.

more.def: A part of a town, city or country, set apart for a purpose.
examples: Several schools in the district share a bus system.
The shopping district is full of stores.
The district around the old market is very busy.

easy.def: To bother someone or break their quiet.
examples: Do not disturb the baby.
The noise disturbed me.
Please do not disturb the sleeping cat.

more.def: To interrupt someone or to spoil the quiet or calm of something.
examples: Please do not disturb the baby while she sleeps.
The loud music disturbed our reading.
Do not disturb the nest in the tree.

easy.def: To jump into water head first.
examples: I dive into the pool.
She dove off the board.
The seal dived.

more.def: To jump into water with your head first, or to go deep under water.
examples: She dived into the pool with a splash.
The seal dove deep under the waves.
The swimmers dove for coins at the bottom.

easy.def: Splitting a number into equal groups.
examples: We learned division in math.
Division is the opposite of multiplication.
Six divided by two is a division.

more.def: The act of splitting a number into equal parts in math, or of separating something into parts.
examples: In math class we practiced long division.
The division of the cake gave everyone a fair slice.
A fence made a clear division between the two yards.

easy.def: When two married people end their marriage.
examples: His parents got a divorce.
A divorce can be hard.
Her parents had a divorce.

more.def: The legal ending of a marriage.
examples: His parents got a divorce last year.
A divorce can be hard for a family.
The judge granted the divorce.
